question: G3 found per-tile operational S~1.2x (launch-bound) despite intrinsic math gamma 6-10x. Does batching/fusion recover the headroom? (the G4 fusion question)
method: Torch batchability probe on A100 (reuses G1 tiles + verified teacher/student ports). Batch B tiles' pixels into ONE student predict call (B*256 px, shared rank-R params, params created once, no H2D in loop). Measure student per-tile latency vs B.
intrinsic_gamma_note: Run-to-run GPU-state sensitivity: room run1=6.35, room run2=14.5, garden=10.46. Range 6-14x; all > assumed 2-4x. Intrinsic gamma is GPU-clock-sensitive (not clock-locked); report as range, not point.
NOT_reported_as_speedup: S_batch = teacher_per_tile / student_per_tile is NOT reported: teacher is B separate noisy calls (0.08ms at B<=4 but 0.38ms at B>=8, a measurement artifact), making S_batch asymmetric/unreliable. Only the student batching curve (clean, single-call) is used.
finding: Student per-tile latency drops ~181x from B=1 (0.0696ms, launch-bound) to B=256 (0.00038ms, intrinsic per-element). The CGT student eval is HIGHLY batchable: launch overhead amortizes to near-zero by B~128-256. Therefore a renderer that batches many cells per kernel launch (as a fused CGT kernel would) approaches the intrinsic per-element cost, and the per-tile 1.2x is a launch-granularity artifact, NOT a fundamental limit.
implication: Batching/fusion is the viable G4 path to recover the 6-14x math headroom. CAVEAT: this is a torch batchability probe, NOT a fused CGT CUDA kernel vs gsplat's fused rasterizer (the true G4 microbenchmark). The teacher/Gaussian baseline must also be batch-amortized (gsplat already is, being fused) for the end-to-end S to approach intrinsic gamma.
scope_caveat: torch reference; no spatial tree / cost selector / fused CUDA kernel; GPU not clock-locked (intrinsic gamma variance).
